Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Rick Mc Leod <rxm@mda.com.au> wrote:
>This 'Golden Rule of Card Ownership': Maybe I read more intent (or common
>sense) into it than as written, but I was herein faced with the following
>situation. X has carried a vote for Rumors of Gehenna on X and myself.
>X is also hurting with one V contested, Tatiana in torpor, and one
>(bloodless) V under Masq. Endangered. I use Grave Robbing on Tatiana.
>Next turn, I oust my prey. Defenseless X is ousted seconds later on the 
>next bleed. (5 players remain). X invokes the "Golden Rule' to revoke
>Tatiana and Gehenna from the game.

Yup, that's how it works.

>There's: "Wait a minute: The <controlled thing> still exists. Why don't
>I just pull one out of my spares, and you can take your card."

Because that's not what the GR says.  If you are ousted, all cards you
own are burned and returned to you; whether the people still in the game
own any replacement cards is irrelevant.

>What is WotC's position on the GR? Also, would Gehenna necessarily
>disappear just because of the card. I thought it was a "condition", 
>more than a permanent card. 

It meets one of the three criteria for staying in play rather than merely
being an effect (namely, it can be burned by calling a vote), so it does
stick around, and is burned if its owner is ousted.  This would not apply
to, say, Kindred Restructure, which doesn't meet any of the criteria for
sticking around, so is just an "effect" and would apply even after
the CE's owner is ousted.

Again, the three criteria to see whether something stays in play vs.
just being an effect:

1.  The card is a location, skill, retainer, ally, or equipment.
2.  The card says to place it on something (typically a vampire).
3.  The card gives some condition for being burnt or stolen.

Messages.Author: CHRISTOPHER M. ACKNEY
Messages.Body:
I heard this from somewhere, but I'm hoping to have a more official ruling
on it (Tom, any ideas?).  

Someone uses a mass destruction spell (Wrath of God, Nevinyrral's Disk, etc)
Could one use various enchantments and abilities such as regeneration to
save them.  I can only remember an example of a regenerating craw wurm or
something, and the player regenerated the craw wurm, keeping it in play 
(though the enchantment was lost).  Just curious (and tired of WoG and the
disk).

Chris

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
CHRISTOPHER M. ACKNEY <cs911035@ariel.cs.yorku.ca> wrote:
>Someone uses a mass destruction spell (Wrath of God, Nevinyrral's Disk, etc)
>Could one use various enchantments and abilities such as regeneration to
>save them.  I can only remember an example of a regenerating craw wurm or
>something, and the player regenerated the craw wurm, keeping it in play 
>(though the enchantment was lost).  Just curious...

Regeneration doesn't care why a creature is going to the graveyard, just
that it is, so can be used against non-targetted effects such as
the Disk.  It cannot be used to save the creature from Wrath of God, but
that's because WoG buries the creature...  it has nothing to do with whether
WoG is targetted or not.
